title: Revolut makes self-hosted GLM the default for about 2,000 engineers after a $300-a-month Claude Code budget showed little impact, and reports paying about a tenth as much
summary: David Abitbol, who leads AI operations at Revolut, told conference audiences that the bank now serves about 2,000 engineers with the open-weight GLM model on 56 NVIDIA B200 GPUs, and that open models have become its default for coding agents. Revolut launched Claude Code in January 2026 with a budget of $300 per engineer per month. He says that was not enough to last an engineer the month. From April 2026 it offered self-hosted GLM with the promise of unlimited tokens, keeping Anthropic and OpenAI models as a smaller, budgeted option for the hardest problems. He reports a blended cost of $0.30 per million tokens, about a tenth of the earlier cost, on a flat invoice, and says tuning alone cut time to first token by 88% with the GPU count unchanged.
source: AI Engineer NYC 2026 (conference talk), also given at NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026
observer: David Abitbol, who leads AI operations at Revolut, describing Revolut's own AI rollout, costs and engineering metrics in two conference talks
leadTimeEstimate: ~12-24 months before open models as the default for coding agents are common in large engineering organisations
whyItMatters: **Budgets shape what agents do** — Abitbol's account suggests a tight per-engineer limit keeps agents on the work engineers think is worth the money.
**Flat bills change the question** — where others are tightening per-engineer caps, Revolut moved routine work to capacity with a flat invoice.
**Frontier becomes the exception** — a regulated bank treats open models as the default and keeps frontier models as a budgeted option for the hardest problems.
recommendedActions: **Analyse potential of open weight models** — review the costs, engineering effort, and capacity requirements before committing to self-hosting.
risksAndCaveats: **Vendor-linked source** — the figures are Revolut's own, the NVIDIA session was presented by Together AI, and a slide names Together alongside the GPUs without explaining its role.
